assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-based amplification framework fundamentally changed macro-finance analysis of credit cycles and policy transmission.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the central collateral mechanism, while Gertler made financial-accelerator models influential in modern macroeconomics.
assessment.maturity: Its mechanisms have been extensively developed, quantified, and applied through major financial disruptions.
uncertainties: The contribution spans related models with several consequential contributors, making a three-person allocation necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on liquidity, funding constraints, and asset prices provided a durable account of a central source of financial instability.
assessment.attribution: Amihud established foundational liquidity measurement, while Brunnermeier and Pedersen clarified the interaction of market and funding liquidity.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have broad empirical and institutional relevance and were strongly validated by crisis-era experience.
uncertainties: The intellectual lineage of liquidity research is extensive and credit allocation across measurement, theory, and applications is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work established household balance sheets and mortgage debt as essential for understanding consumption, crises, and macroeconomic recovery.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi made the empirical case for debt-driven downturns, with Campbell providing foundational analysis of household finance and mortgage credit.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated across settings and is now central to macro-finance research and policy discussion.
uncertainties: The precise division between this contribution and wider credit-cycle research remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Legal-origins research transformed the empirical study of investor protection, corporate ownership, and financial development.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, and Vishny formed the core collaboration; the three proposed names capture much of its empirical and conceptual leadership.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has generated a vast literature and has reshaped research in corporate finance, law, and development.
uncertainties: Credit exclusion is especially difficult because Robert W. Vishny was integral to the core work.
The strength and interpretation of legal-origin causal claims remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical industrial organization made demand estimation and analysis of market power, mergers, and dynamic competition operational.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Pakes, and Bresnahan were pivotal architects of the framework, though the listed set reflects a broad and intertwined research program.
assessment.maturity: These tools have become standard across industrial organization and competition-policy analysis.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping contains more major contributors than can receive the prize jointly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm-heterogeneity trade models recast the analysis of selection, productivity, and welfare gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the landmark heterogeneous-firm framework; Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in modern trade theory, quantitative work, and empirical analysis.
uncertainties: The breadth of the heterogeneous-firm literature complicates assignment of a single prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work gave rigorous economic foundations for treating natural capital, exhaustible resources, and biodiversity as central components of welfare and wealth.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal jointly made foundational contributions to resource economics and intergenerational evaluation.
assessment.maturity: The work has had a long scholarly life and rising relevance in environmental accounting and policy.
uncertainties: The direct empirical and policy consensus around inclusive-wealth measures remains less settled than the foundational theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Information design and Bayesian persuasion created a powerful general framework for analyzing strategic communication and the design of information environments.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Bergemann pioneered persuasion and information design, while Morris made foundational contributions to strategic information economics.
assessment.maturity: The framework has spread rapidly through theory and applied work in markets, platforms, and public policy.
uncertainties: Its relatively recent expansion leaves less time to assess its ultimate empirical and policy impact.
